change.title: pr-38446-flat
change.description: Implement recovery key support for user storage providers
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: Recovery-codes test only covers the happy path
findings.body: `testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin` sets up codes and logs in once with code #0. It never submits a wrong code, so the new `isValid` branch in `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage` (line 340) is only tested for acceptance. The fixture accepts any code in the stored list and never consumes one. `getNextRecoveryAuthnCode()` therefore always returns number 0, and the code-consumption and `allCodesUsed` paths in `RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator` (lines 85-92) are not exercised for user-storage credentials. Add a negative assertion (an invalid code is rejected) so a broken validation branch cannot pass.

findings.title: Copied delayed-authenticator step and typo'd alias add nothing to this test
findings.body: The flow setup is copied from `RecoveryAuthnCodesAuthenticatorTest` (lines 136-137 there). It adds a `delayed-authenticator` with `delay=0`, and the alias `delayed-suthenticator-config` has a typo. This test needs no delay, so the extra execution and the `delay` parameter of `configureBrowserFlowWithRecoveryAuthnCodes` can be dropped. The method is also package-private and takes `testingClient`, which is already a field.

findings.title: Class doc says the provider stays unchanged, but it now implements newer SPI
findings.body: The class Javadoc says this provider was created in Keycloak 4.8.3 and that future versions should work without code changes. The PR adds `getCredentials` (a newer `CredentialInputUpdater` method), recovery-code support and OTP ids. The fixture therefore no longer represents a 4.8.3 provider, and the backwards-compatibility guarantee it was written to check is weaker. Either put the recovery-code support in a separate test provider or update the Javadoc to say the fixture is extended.

findings.title: New getCredentials override changes the OTP fixture, and recovery codes get no id
findings.body: `getCredentials` now also returns the OTP credential, which changes what `getFederatedCredentialsStream` yields for the existing OTP tests. The recovery credential is built with `createFromValues`, which gives it a null id. `CredentialDeleteHelper` (services/.../util/CredentialDeleteHelper.java:64) finds federated credentials by id, so that credential can never be matched or deleted. `recoveryCodes.getId()` is already generated at line 195, so it could be set on the returned model. Also, the `IOException` catch at line 244 swallows the exception, so a deserialization failure is silent.

findings.title: Unrelated re-indentation of getConfigurableAuthenticatorFactory
findings.body: Lines 76-85 only change indentation (a whitespace-only diff). The same is true of the whitespace-only edits in `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageTest` (lines 328 and 467-468) and in `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage` (lines 61 and 95). They add noise to blame and review and are unrelated to the feature.

findings.title: Optional is wrapped and then unwrapped with get()
findings.body: `credentialModelOpt.get()` throws a bare `NoSuchElementException` if no credential is found, exactly as the old `findFirst().get()` did. The `Optional` local adds nothing. If the call is kept, use `orElseThrow` with a message that names the user and credential type, so the failure is diagnosable. This matters more now that the credential may come from either the user storage or the local store.

contracts.action: Recovery codes are created through CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential: first offered to the user storage as a plaintext JSON list, otherwise stored locally
contracts.equivalent_path: CredentialHelper.createOTPCredential (same file, line 92), which tries user.credentialManager().updateCredential and falls back to the local provider's createCredential
contracts.before_after: Before, RecoveryAuthnCodesAction called the local provider's createCredential directly. Now updateCredential is tried first; UserCredentialManager.updateCredential (model/storage/.../UserCredentialManager.java:83-99) asks the federation provider and then the local CredentialInputUpdaters. RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider is not a CredentialInputUpdater (services/.../RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.java:19-20), so local users get false and fall through to createCredential, as before. The OTP sibling does the same dispatch.
contracts.visible_effect: Users from a provider that supports the type get their codes stored in the provider; all other users behave as before.
contracts.failure_mode: A JsonSerialization IOException becomes a RuntimeException, which is acceptable for a List<String>. If the storage returns true, any existing local recovery credential is not deleted, whereas the local createCredential path deletes the old one (RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.java:39-40). getCredential prefers the federated credential, so the stale local one is ignored but remains.

contracts.action: RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential looks for the recovery credential in federated storage first, then locally; the form authenticator and the login bean now use it
contracts.equivalent_path: The previous direct calls to getStoredCredentialsByTypeStream(TYPE).findFirst() in RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator and RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean
contracts.before_after: getFederatedCredentialsStream (UserCredentialManager.java:129-146) returns the provider's getCredentials for federated users, otherwise an empty stream; the default getCredentials is empty (CredentialInputUpdater.java:50-52). Local users therefore behave as before. Other local readers such as RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.isValid and isConfiguredFor still read only local credentials; the manager's isValid/isConfiguredFor check the user storage first, so they are consistent.
contracts.visible_effect: The login form shows the next code number and the authenticator marks the credential used, for user-storage credentials.
contracts.failure_mode: For a storage-owned credential that has all codes used, the authenticator calls removeStoredCredentialById on the federated store (RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator.java:85-88). That does not remove the credential from the provider, and the id may be null. The user is then sent to CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES. The fixture never reaches this case, because it does not consume codes.
